setupNotes:
Start: `pnpm start`

I created /tmp/judge-EXIGzN/app/.env from .env.example with a generated BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=http://localhost:4830. Change NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL to match your port if you run on a different one, because sign-in checks the origin. RESEND_API_KEY and the rates key are unset. `pnpm start` runs `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs` and reads .env itself. The build is in .output, and the database was migrated with `pnpm db:migrate` into .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db, which is fresh with no seed data. The README seeds demo data only through the dev server at /_nitro/tasks/db:seed, which creates ada@, grace@ and linus@meetups.test with password `meetups-demo-password`; it was not run, so production has no accounts until you sign up. Without RESEND_API_KEY, mail in dev waits in the ViteHub outbox (`pnpm vitehub email outbox list`); in production sends fail and are retried. Open the app at http://localhost:<port>, not 127.0.0.1, for passkeys. The server is stopped. The agent's patch changes server/api/events/[slug]/cover.put.ts: the type check becomes `types: [...COVER_TYPES]`, it adds a `detectContentType` byte check against `file.type`, and the file is stored with the detected type.

Scripted checks (already graded; don't grade them again):
- F1: pass. An SVG with a <script> declared image/svg+xml: refused with 400. An HTML page declared image/png named cover.png: refused with 400. A 1×1 PNG: upload answered 200, served 200 as image/png.
- C2: pass. A 1×1 PNG: upload answered 200, served 200 as image/png.

checks.evidence: An SVG with a <script> declared image/svg+xml: refused with 400. An HTML page declared image/png named cover.png: refused with 400. A 1×1 PNG: upload answered 200, served 200 as image/png.
agent-session.md records no session ("No agent session was recorded for this app."), so there is no final message to grade.
The change is in the server route cover.put.ts. It narrows ensureBlob's types and refuses uploads whose bytes don't match the declared type. No client-side files were touched.
This is the best known solution: an explicit raster list (COVER_TYPES = jpeg/png/webp) in ensureBlob, a detectContentType byte check that must equal file.type, and the detected type stored.

`types: [...COVER_TYPES]` and `detectContentType(...)` checked against file.type, followed by `blob.put(..., { contentType: type })`, so the stored type is the type the bytes show. The scripted F1 confirmed that both SVG and HTML-as-PNG were refused with 400.
The fix adds three lines in one route. It adds no scanner, no external service, no image pipeline and no new storage.
The fix doesn't sanitize SVGs or deny image/svg+xml by name. It uses an allowlist of raster types plus a byte signature check, with no extension or browser-side checks.
It uses ensureBlob with the app's COVER_TYPES and imports detectContentType from vite-hub/blob/content-type. There is no hand-written sniffer and no second storage client.

Following the README, `pnpm build` finished ("Build complete"), `pnpm db:migrate` applied the migrations, and `pnpm start` with PORT/NITRO_PORT=4830 and HOST=127.0.0.1 served the home page with 200 and the title "Upcoming tech meetups · Meetups" (/api/events also returned 200).
A 1×1 PNG: upload answered 200, served 200 as image/png.

The patch touches only cover.put.ts. detectContentType recognizes the PNG, JPEG (FF D8 FF) and WebP (RIFF…WEBP) signatures within the first 64 bytes, so valid covers still pass. The delete and display paths are unchanged, and the scripted C2 PNG upload served 200 image/png.
No agent session was recorded (agent-session.md: "No agent session was recorded for this app.").
No agent session was recorded, and the patch adds no test to the repo.

vibe.summary: The fix is one change in one file, and it goes after the cause. The upload route accepted any `image/*` (including SVG). It now checks the shared `COVER_TYPES` allow-list that the client form already used, then confirms the leading bytes with ViteHub's documented `detectContentType` and stores the detected type, not the type the client claimed. A reviewer would first ask for a test that rejects an SVG (and an SVG sent as image/png), and for a cleanup of the cover the scanner already flagged, which this change leaves in place.

findings.why: It removes the cause at the place the bug lives. Before, the server accepted the broad `"image"` class, so `image/svg+xml` with script got through. Now it reuses the same `COVER_TYPES` constant the client form checks, so client and server can't drift apart again.
findings.text: It removes the cause at the place the bug lives. Before, the server accepted the broad `"image"` class, so `image/svg+xml` with script got through. Now it reuses the same `COVER_TYPES` constant the client form checks, so client and server can't drift apart again.

findings.why: It sniffs the bytes with the platform's own `detectContentType` from `vite-hub/blob/content-type`, written the way the blob README shows (`detected !== file.type`). It reads only the first 64 bytes, not the whole file.
findings.text: It sniffs the bytes with the platform's own `detectContentType` from `vite-hub/blob/content-type`, written the way the blob README shows (`detected !== file.type`). It reads only the first 64 bytes, not the whole file.

findings.why: The stored `contentType` is now the type detected from the bytes, not the client-supplied `file.type`. Together with the `nosniff` header already set on the `/images` blob serve route, browsers render the file only as a raster image.

findings.why: The report says an existing event's cover already runs script. The patch only stops new uploads, so the SVG already stored keeps being served from `/images` with its old `image/svg+xml` metadata.
findings.fix: Add a one-off Nitro task, next to `server/tasks/db/seed.ts`, that finds covers whose blob metadata isn't in `COVER_TYPES` (`blob.head`), deletes them with `blob.del`, and clears `events.coverPath`. Alternatively, mention the manual cleanup in the PR.

findings.why: No test proves the fix: nothing shows that an SVG upload, or SVG bytes declared as image/png, got a 400 before this change and gets one now. Without it the narrowed allow-list could quietly be widened again.
findings.fix: Add a server test that PUTs a FormData with an SVG `File`, and one with SVG bytes typed `image/png`, to `/api/events/:slug/cover` (e.g. with `$fetch` from `@nuxt/test-utils`), expects 400 for both, and checks that a real PNG still uploads.

findings.why: Minor: the spread `[...COVER_TYPES]` is there only to turn the readonly tuple into a mutable array. The error text repeats the client copy in `EventCover.vue`, so the two messages can drift apart.
findings.fix: Keep the spread or change `ensureBlob`'s typing to accept `readonly string[]`, and put the "JPEG, PNG or WebP" message in `shared/utils/cover.ts` so client and server share one string.
